NKJV.1: Now David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And Ahimelech was afraid when he met David, and said to him, “Why are you alone, and no one is with you?”
NKJV.2: So David said to Ahimelech the priest, “The king has ordered me on some business, and said to me, ‘Do not let anyone know anything about the business on which I send you, or what I have commanded you.’ And I have directed my young men to such and such a place.
NKJV.3: Now therefore, what have you on hand? Give me five loaves of bread in my hand, or whatever can be found.”
NKJV.4: And the priest answered David and said, “There is no common bread on hand; but there is holy bread, if the young men have at least kept themselves from women.”
NKJV.5: Then David answered the priest, and said to him, “Truly, women have been kept from us about three days since I came out. And the vessels of the young men are holy, and the bread is in effect common, even though it was consecrated in the vessel this day.”
NKJV.6: So the priest gave him holy bread; for there was no bread there but the showbread which had been taken from before the LORD, in order to put hot bread in its place on the day when it was taken away.
NKJV.7: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD. And his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chief of the herdsmen who belonged to Saul.
NKJV.8: And David said to Ahimelech, “Is there not here on hand a spear or a sword? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s business required haste.”
NKJV.9: So the priest said, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, there it is, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you will take that, take it. For there is no other except that one here.” And David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”
NKJV.10: Then David arose and fled that day from before Saul, and went to Achish the king of Gath.
NKJV.11: And the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David the king of the land? Did they not sing of him to one another in dances, saying: ‘Saul has slain his thousands, And David his ten thousands’?”
NKJV.12: Now David took these words to heart, and was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
NKJV.13: So he changed his behavior before them, pretended madness in their hands, scratched on the doors of the gate, and let his saliva fall down on his beard.
NKJV.14: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you see the man is insane. Why have you brought him to me?
NKJV.15: Have I need of madmen, that you have brought this fellow to play the madman in my presence? Shall this fellow come into my house?”

ESV.1: Then David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And Ahimelech came to meet David, trembling, and said to him, “Why are you alone, and no one with you?”
ESV.2: And David said to Ahimelech the priest, “The king has charged me with a matter and said to me, ‘Let no one know anything of the matter about which I send you, and with which I have charged you.’ I have made an appointment with the young men for such and such a place.
ESV.3: Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever is here.”
ESV.4: And the priest answered David, “I have no common bread on hand, but there is holy bread — if the young men have kept themselves from women.”
ESV.5: And David answered the priest, “Truly women have been kept from us as always when I go on an expedition. The vessels of the young men are holy even when it is an ordinary journey. How much more today will their vessels be holy?”
ESV.6: So the priest gave him the holy bread, for there was no bread there but the bread of the Presence, which is removed from before the LORD, to be replaced by hot bread on the day it is taken away.
ESV.7: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD. His name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul's herdsmen.
ESV.8: Then David said to Ahimelech, “Then have you not here a spear or a sword at hand? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's business required haste.”
ESV.9: And the priest said, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah, behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you will take that, take it, for there is none but that here.” And David said, “There is none like that; give it to me.”
ESV.10: And David rose and fled that day from Saul and went to Achish the king of Gath.
ESV.11: And the servants of Achish said to him, “Is not this David the king of the land? Did they not sing to one another of him in dances, ‘Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands’?”
ESV.12: And David took these words to heart and was much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
ESV.13: So he changed his behavior before them and pretended to be insane in their hands and made marks on the doors of the gate and let his spittle run down his beard.
ESV.14: Then Achish said to his servants, “Behold, you see the man is mad. Why then have you brought him to me?
ESV.15: Do I lack madmen, that you have brought this fellow to behave as a madman in my presence? Shall this fellow come into my house?”

NLT.1: David went to the town of Nob to see Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech trembled when he saw him. “Why are you alone?” he asked. “Why is no one with you?”
NLT.2: “The king has sent me on a private matter,” David said. “He told me not to tell anyone why I am here. I have told my men where to meet me later.
NLT.3: Now, what is there to eat? Give me five loaves of bread or anything else you have.”
NLT.4: “We don’t have any regular bread,” the priest replied. “But there is the holy bread, which you can have if your young men have not slept with any women recently.”
NLT.5: “Don’t worry,” David replied. “I never allow my men to be with women when we are on a campaign. And since they stay clean even on ordinary trips, how much more on this one!”
NLT.6: Since there was no other food available, the priest gave him the holy bread — the Bread of the Presence that was placed before the LORD in the Tabernacle. It had just been replaced that day with fresh bread.
NLT.7: Now Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s chief herdsman, was there that day, having been detained before the LORD.
NLT.8: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or sword? The king’s business was so urgent that I didn’t even have time to grab a weapon!”
NLT.9: “I only have the sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the valley of Elah,” the priest replied. “It is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. Take that if you want it, for there is nothing else here.” “There is nothing like it!” David replied. “Give it to me!”
NLT.10: So David escaped from Saul and went to King Achish of Gath.
NLT.11:
But the officers of Achish were unhappy about his being there. “Isn’t this David, the king of the land?” they asked. “Isn’t he the one the people honor with dances, singing, ‘Saul has killed his thousands,
and David his ten thousands’?”
NLT.12: David heard these comments and was very afraid of what King Achish of Gath might do to him.
NLT.13: So he pretended to be insane, scratching on doors and drooling down his beard.
NLT.14: Finally, King Achish said to his men, “Must you bring me a madman?
NLT.15: We already have enough of them around here! Why should I let someone like this be my guest?”

AMP.1: Then David went to Nob to Ahimelech the priest; and Ahimelech came trembling [in fear] to meet David and said to him, "Why are you alone, and no one with you?"
AMP.2: David said to Ahimelech the priest, "The king has commissioned me with a matter and has told me, 'Let no one know anything about the matter for which I am sending you and with which I have commissioned you. I have directed the young men to a certain place.'
AMP.3: Now what [food] do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found."
AMP.4: The priest answered David, "There is no ordinary (unconsecrated) bread on hand, but there is consecrated bread; [you may have it] if only the young men have kept themselves from women."
AMP.5: David answered the priest, "Be assured that women have been kept from us in these three days since I set out, and the bodies of the young men were consecrated (ceremonially clean), although it was an ordinary (unconsecrated) journey; so how much more will their vessels be holy today?"
AMP.6: So the priest gave him the consecrated bread; for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence which was removed from before the LORD in order to put hot bread in its place when it was taken away.
AMP.7: Now one of Saul's servants was there that day, detained before the LORD; his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul's shepherds.
AMP.8: David said to Ahimelech, "Do you not have a sword or spear here on hand? For I brought neither my sword nor my [other] weapons with me, because the king's business was urgent."
AMP.9: Then the priest said, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod; if you would take it for yourself, do so. For there is no other here except for it." And David said, "There is none like that; give it to me."
AMP.10: Then David arose and fled from Saul that day, and went to Achish king of Gath.
AMP.11:
The servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David the king of the land? Did they not sing in praise of this one as they danced, saying,
'Saul has slain his thousands,
And David his ten thousands'?"
AMP.12: David took these words to heart and was greatly afraid of Achish king of Gath.
AMP.13: So [fearing for his life] he changed his behavior in their sight, and acted insanely in their hands, and he scribbled on the doors of the gate, and drooled on his beard.
AMP.14: Then Achish said to his servants, "Look, you see that the man is insane. Why have you brought him to me?
AMP.15: Do I lack madmen, that you bring this one to behave like a madman in my presence? Shall this one come into my house?"

WEB.6: So the priest gave him holy bread; for there was no bread there but the show bread that was taken from before Yahweh, to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.

MSG.1:
David went on his way and Jonathan returned to town.
David went to Nob, to Ahimelech the Priest. Ahimelech was alarmed as he went out to greet David: "What are you doing here all by yourself—and not a soul with you?"
MSG.2: David answered Ahimelech the Priest, "The king sent me on a mission and gave strict orders: 'This is top secret—not a word of this to a soul.' I've arranged to meet up with my men in a certain place.
MSG.3: Now, what's there here to eat? Do you have five loaves of bread? Give me whatever you can scrounge up!"
MSG.4: "I don't have any regular bread on hand," said the priest. "I only have holy bread. If your men have not slept with women recently, it's yours."
MSG.5: David said, "None of us has touched a woman. I always do it this way when I'm on a mission: My men abstain from sex. Even when it is an ordinary mission we do that—how much more on this holy mission."
MSG.6: So the priest gave them the holy bread. It was the only bread he had, Bread of the Presence that had been removed from God's presence and replaced by fresh bread at the same time.
MSG.7: One of Saul's officials was present that day keeping a religious vow. His name was Doeg the Edomite. He was chief of Saul's shepherds.
MSG.8: David asked Ahimelech, "Do you have a spear or sword of any kind around here? I didn't have a chance to grab my weapons. The king's mission was urgent and I left in a hurry."
MSG.9: The priest said, "The sword of Goliath, the Philistine you killed at Oak Valley—that's here! It's behind the Ephod wrapped in a cloth. If you want it, take it. There's nothing else here."
MSG.10:
"Oh," said David, "there's no sword like that! Give it to me!"
And at that, David shot out of there, running for his life from Saul. He went to Achish, king of Gath.
MSG.11:
When the servants of Achish saw him, they said, "Can this be David, the famous David? Is this the one they sing of at their dances?
Saul kills by the thousand,
David by the ten thousand!"
MSG.12: When David realized that he had been recognized, he panicked, fearing the worst from Achish, king of Gath.
MSG.13: So right there, while they were looking at him, he pretended to go crazy, pounding his head on the city gate and foaming at the mouth, spit dripping from his beard.
MSG.14: Achish took one look at him and said to his servants, "Can't you see he's crazy? Why did you let him in here?
MSG.15: Don't you think I have enough crazy people to put up with as it is without adding another? Get him out of here!"

NRSVCE.3: Now then, what have you at hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever is here.”
NRSVCE.4: The priest answered David, “I have no ordinary bread at hand, only holy bread — provided that the young men have kept themselves from women.”
NRSVCE.5: David answered the priest, “Indeed women have been kept from us as always when I go on an expedition; the vessels of the young men are holy even when it is a common journey; how much more today will their vessels be holy?”
NRSVCE.6: So the priest gave him the holy bread; for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which is removed from before the LORD, to be replaced by hot bread on the day it is taken away.
NRSVCE.7: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD; his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul’s shepherds.
NRSVCE.8: David said to Ahimelech, “Is there no spear or sword here with you? I did not bring my sword or my weapons with me, because the king’s business required haste.”
NRSVCE.9: The priest said, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the valley of Elah, is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod; if you will take that, take it, for there is none here except that one.” David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”
NRSVCE.10: David rose and fled that day from Saul; he went to King Achish of Gath.
NRSVCE.11:
The servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David the king of the land? Did they not sing to one another of him in dances, ‘Saul has killed his thousands,
and David his ten thousands’?”
NRSVCE.12: David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of King Achish of Gath.
NRSVCE.13: So he changed his behavior before them; he pretended to be mad when in their presence. He scratched marks on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle run down his beard.
NRSVCE.14: Achish said to his servants, “Look, you see the man is mad; why then have you brought him to me?
NRSVCE.15: Do I lack madmen, that you have brought this fellow to play the madman in my presence? Shall this fellow come into my house?”

NET.1: (21:1) Then David got up and left, while Jonathan went back to the city. (21:2) David went to Ahimelech the priest in Nob. Ahimelech was shaking with fear when he met David, and said to him, “Why are you by yourself with no one accompanying you?”
NET.2: David replied to Ahimelech the priest, “The king instructed me to do something, but he said to me, ‘Don’t let anyone know the reason I am sending you or the instructions I have given you.’ I have told my soldiers to wait at a certain place.
NET.3: Now what do you have at your disposal? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found.”
NET.4: The priest replied to David, “I don’t have any ordinary bread at my disposal. Only holy bread is available, and then only if your soldiers have abstained from sexual relations with women.”
NET.5: David said to the priest, “Certainly women have been kept away from us, just as on previous occasions when I have set out. The soldiers’ equipment is holy, even on an ordinary journey. How much more so will they be holy today, along with their equipment!”
NET.6: So the priest gave him holy bread, for there was no bread there other than the bread of the Presence. It had been removed from before the LORD in order to replace it with hot bread on the day it had been taken away.
NET.7: (One of Saul’s servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. His name was Doeg the Edomite, who was in charge of Saul’s shepherds.)
NET.8: David said to Ahimelech, “Is there no sword or spear here at your disposal? I don’t have my own sword or equipment in hand due to the urgency of the king’s instructions.”
NET.9: The priest replied, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the valley of Elah, is wrapped in a garment behind the ephod. If you wish, take it for yourself. Other than that, there’s nothing here.” David said, “There’s nothing like it! Give it to me!”
NET.10: So on that day David arose and fled from Saul. He went to King Achish of Gath.
NET.11: The servants of Achish said to him, “Isn’t this David, the king of the land? Isn’t he the one that they sing about when they dance, saying, ‘Saul struck down his thousands, But David his tens of thousands’?”
NET.12: David thought about what they said and was very afraid of King Achish of Gath.
NET.13: He altered his behavior in their presence. Since he was in their power, he pretended to be insane, making marks on the doors of the gate and letting his saliva run down his beard.
NET.14: Achish said to his servants, “Look at this madman! Why did you bring him to me?
NET.15: Do I have a shortage of fools, that you have brought me this man to display his insanity in front of me? Should this man enter my house?”

NIV.1:
David at Nob
David went to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech trembled when he met him, and asked, “Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?”
NIV.2: David answered Ahimelech the priest, “The king charged me with a certain matter and said to me, ‘No one is to know anything about your mission and your instructions.’ As for my men, I have told them to meet me at a certain place.
NIV.3: Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever you can find.”
NIV.4: But the priest answered David, “I don’t have any ordinary bread on hand; however, there is some consecrated bread here—provided the men have kept themselves from women.”
NIV.5: David replied, “Indeed women have been kept from us, as usual whenever I set out. The men’s things are holy even on missions that are not holy. How much more so today!”
NIV.6: So the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence that had been removed from before the Lord and replaced by hot bread on the day it was taken away.
NIV.7: Now one of Saul’s servants was there that day, detained before the Lord; he was Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s head shepherd.
NIV.8: David asked Ahimelech, “Don’t you have a spear or a sword here? I haven’t brought my sword or any other weapon, because the king’s business was urgent.”
NIV.9:
The priest replied, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here; it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want it, take it; there is no sword here but that one.”
David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”
NIV.10:
David at Gath
That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.
NIV.11:
But the servants of Achish said to him, “Isn’t this David, the king of the land? Isn’t he the one they sing about in their dances:
“‘Saul has slain his thousands,
and David his tens of thousands’?”
NIV.12: David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish king of Gath.
NIV.13: So he pretended to be insane in their presence; and while he was in their hands he acted like a madman, making marks on the doors of the gate and letting saliva run down his beard.
NIV.14: Achish said to his servants, “Look at the man! He is insane! Why bring him to me?
NIV.15: Am I so short of madmen that you have to bring this fellow here to carry on like this in front of me? Must this man come into my house?”
